parsedVerdict.reasoning: The domain-layer file holds a concrete, Map-backed repository instead of a repository interface. The class owns the storage state (`private orders: Map<string, Order>`) and implements storing, lookup and query logic in save, getById, getByState and getAll. That is a persistence responsibility, which belongs to the infrastructure layer. The domain layer should only declare the repository contract and leave the implementation to infrastructure. The graph shows application use cases injecting this concrete class directly, which confirms that the persistence code sits in the domain layer instead of behind a port.
